about: 59 lines written by hand, one at a time, for the Illness Test Graph's patient, NOT from the frames of flesh-out.py, each with the tag a careful reader would give it (null: a plain note). Used by tools/graph/measure-tags.js to see how tag suggestion does on writing it has not seen the twin of. Nothing here is written into the graph.

lines.text: Woke up with my hands buzzing like they'd fallen asleep, and it took until mid-morning to settle.
Mouth feels like sandpaper, even water stings.
Bit of a queasy morning, managed dry toast only. [[Nausea]]
Can't be bothered to do anything. Sat in the chair most of the afternoon.
Stabbing pain low down on the right at about eleven, gone by lunch.
Third visit to the loo this morning and nothing solid.
Everything I eat tastes of tin foil.
Cold wind on my face today and it felt like needles.
Lay awake until four, brain going round and round.
Dizzy when I got up from the sofa, had to hold the wall.
Hair coming out in the shower in handfuls.
Appetite has gone again, ate three spoonfuls of soup.
Feel flat and low today, nothing to do with the weather.
My trousers are hanging off me now.
Ruth and I spent the evening going over the options for Christmas; she wants the children here.
[[Amara Okoro]] phoned from Leeds in a state about her job but ended up asking about me.
[[Lena Park]] popped in to look at the dressing and chatted about her allotment.
Dr. Alvarez's office called to confirm they had my forms.
Zoë on the phone for ten minutes about what's normal after the drip.
Had a long chat with Graham over a pint of lemonade; he's been through something similar with his brother.
[[Tunde Okoro]] on video, the connection kept freezing.
Sam rang to say the book group will meet here this month so I don't have to travel.
Grace left a voicemail and I rang her back; she was crying again.
Neighbour Joan stopped me at the gate to ask how it's going.
Priya at the pharmacy explained the new tablets while I waited.
Peter from the library sent a message; the whole team signed a card.
Appointment with [[Dr. Julia Fenn]] this morning, she looked at my fingers and tested my grip.
Dr. Brooks gave me the flu jab and checked my blood pressure while she was at it.
Went in to see [[Dr. Mei Chen]], who wants to hold off on cycle 6 until the counts improve.
Clinic review at Northgate; Dr. Fenn examined the line site and approved me for the next cycle.
Dr. Patel's follow-up at Riverside. Scar looks good, no hernia.
Telephone consultation with Dr. Brooks about the cough, sounds like a chest infection.
Saw [[Dr. Sofia Alvarez]] again about the polyp results.
Dr. Okonkwo, the locum, checked my chest and listened for a long time.
Dr. Watanabe came to the bed before theatre and ticked through his list of questions.
Scan booked for the 12th of November.
Blood test Monday, fasting not needed.
Dr. Chen's clinic is on the 18th, bring the list of questions.
Dentist at 10:30 on Friday.
Flu jab appointment next week.
Cycle 6 pencilled in for the 18th of November.
Physio again Thursday afternoon.
Results appointment in two weeks.
Cycle 5 finished this afternoon; the drip took four hours because the line was slow.
Back from chemo number five, pump in my bag and a cup of tea in my hand.
Pruned the roses before the first frost.
Radio 4 had a good programme about bridges.
Bought a second-hand typewriter at the market, keys all stick.
The new neighbours have a very loud dog.
Finished the crossword in record time.
[[Ruth Okoro]]'s choir sang at the care home.
Left the umbrella on the bus again.
Made marmalade; the whole house smells of oranges.
Library: reshelved the poetry section, found a first edition under a pile of newspapers.
Listening to old jazz records and not thinking about anything.
Walked to the end of the pier and back. Sea was grey.
Dinner at [[Graham Whitlock]]'s, we watched the match.
Rain all day, read three chapters of the new Pat Barker.
Wrote Christmas cards for the first time in years.
